title: Understanding Bernoulli Sampling
text: Bernoulli sampling is a probabilistic method where each row in the table has a fixed probability of being included in the sample. This means that the number of rows in the sample can vary each time you run the query.

title: Exploring the LIMIT Clause
text: The LIMIT clause in SQL is used to specify the number of records you want to retrieve from a query. It doesn't provide any probabilistic sampling but rather a fixed number of rows.

hintAnswer: Bernoulli sampling provides a probabilistic sample, while LIMIT retrieves a fixed number of rows.
title: Comparing Sampling Methods
text: Which of the following statements is true about Bernoulli sampling and the LIMIT clause?
choices: Bernoulli sampling provides a probabilistic sample, while LIMIT retrieves a fixed number of rows.
LIMIT provides a probabilistic sample, while Bernoulli retrieves a fixed number of rows.
Both Bernoulli and LIMIT provide probabilistic samples.
Both Bernoulli and LIMIT retrieve a fixed number of rows.

title: Interpreting the Output
text: When you use TABLESAMPLE, the output can give you an idea of the distribution of data across the entire table, as it randomly selects rows based on a probability. This can hint at the overall size and structure of the table.
